raw_comment:
1. The section of Texas that is attached to Mexico was suffering a serious drought. The state on the coasts were suffering little to no drought. It seems the lower parts of Texas were hit the worst when it comes to the drought. The landlocked states such as Wyoming, North Dakota, and states in said region were also significantly affected by drought. Ohio although having a great lake was considerably affected by drought which extended into West Virginia
2.Why was the drought worse for Texas but not New Mexico considering they are very close to each other in a geographical sense? Why is there just a blank spot in the middle of Colorado considering its a more landlocked state?
3.These drought patterns could forecast a continuation in the pattern that they show as the dryness only gets worse or a change that is to come in the near future, as my state isn't heavily afflicted by this as other states are it might worsen or get better depending if the weather shifts or not
4. Haunted by Drought: How the Unyielding Dry Spell is Trick-or-Treating on Our Resources
